attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his signed post. The following block quote is his own earlier writing.

semantics.note: Keeps the claimed cause (high and rising costs) and the effect (no profit lever). The 'software economics don't make sense' clause is folded in but not lost.

contract.note: In his own context, 'profit lever' means turning profitable after growth, so testing it as operating profit through scale is a fair, ordinary reading. Reading 'costs' as a share of revenue rather than absolute spend is an evaluator choice, and the contract flags it.

evidence.note: In its S-1, Anthropic reports $1.0B GAAP operating income for Q2 2026 because revenue growth outpaced expense growth. This is a company filing.
The H1 2026 operating loss shrank to $693M on $16.3B revenue, and the filing credits compute efficiency. Compute of about $8.9B is roughly 55% of revenue, so its share fell.
Net losses continue, but mostly from non-cash fair-value charges, and Anthropic warns profitability may not last. This limits but does not cancel the operating-profit result.

reviews.rationale: The contract's contradiction test is met. A leading model provider, Anthropic, reached GAAP operating profit in Q2 2026 as revenue outgrew costs, and compute fell as a share of revenue. Absolute compute spending did keep rising, but under the contract that alone doesn't support the claim. Caveats: this is one quarter, H1 2026 was still an operating loss, and there's no evidence on resellers like Replit or Cursor.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: The aside 'it isn't [profitable], and will burn billions this year' is captured faithfully. 'This year' is calendar 2025, given the September 2025 post date.

contract.note: Reading 'billions' as at least $2B is ordinary. Every reading of 'burn' (operating cash used, cash outflow, operating loss) exceeds $2B, so the choice doesn't change the result.

evidence.note: The S-1 reports a $42.0B net loss for 2025, so Anthropic was unprofitable. Most of it was a non-cash fair-value charge.
The S-1 cash-flow table shows $2.64B used in operating activities in 2025 and $3.08B in investing. Operating cash use alone exceeds $2B.
Per The Next Web citing Reuters, the 2025 operating loss was $8.06B, which matches the S-1.

reviews.rationale: The 2025 horizon has passed. Anthropic's filing shows a net loss, an operating loss of about $8B, and about $2.6B of operating cash used in 2025. That is billions burned on any reasonable reading, and the company was not profitable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his signed post.

semantics.note: Faithful to the demand clause. The GDP-growth clause is set aside, which is appropriate since it is a separate claim.

contract.note: Reading the line as 'no meaningful demand' rather than literally zero users is fair and ordinary. Choosing August 2025 as the window is the evaluator's choice but reasonable for a present-tense statement. The 'let alone at scale' part can't be resolved, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: OpenAI said on 2025-08-07 that nearly 700M people use ChatGPT weekly and 5M paid business users exist. This is a company disclosure.
Ramp's independent spend data shows paid business AI adoption at 44.5% in August 2025. This is a panel sample, not every business.

reviews.rationale: The core claim, that there really isn't any demand for AI in general, is contradicted for August 2025. Hundreds of millions of weekly users and paid adoption at about 44% of firms in Ramp's sample show substantial demand. 'Let alone at scale' is an intensifier built on that base claim. Whether demand justifies the investment is unresolved, but that doesn't rescue the general claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his signed post.

semantics.note: Captures both the present claim and the unlimited 'never, ever arriving' forecast. No deadline is given.

contract.note: His context ('illusion of demand', capacity hoarding) supports reading demand as sustainable demand that pays for the buildout. That threshold is the evaluator's, not the speaker's, so interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: Ramp's August 2026 data shows substantial paid adoption, but growth is slowing and spending per employee fell. It doesn't show receipts covering the buildout.
CNBC, citing unnamed sources, reports OpenAI 2025 revenue of $13.1B and cash burn of $8B. This shows real receipts but continued funding needs at one company.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended 'never' forecast. The contract's early-resolution test, sustained demand shown to support the service and infrastructure economics, isn't met by the packet. Paid adoption and revenue exist, but neither item shows receipts covering the buildout. Nothing here could support 'never' either.
